title: Hardware-backed keys rollout plan and terraform notes (v0.1 draft)
content:
Status: draft (working notes for private deployment security team)

High-level summary:
This doc captures a pragmatic rollout plan to introduce hardware-backed key management across private (VPC/on-prem) Redwood deployments, plus concrete Terraform module notes and upgrade steps for services that currently use software KMS/Vault-only secrets. Goal is to achieve an HSM-backed envelope encryption model with auditable key lifecycle, minimal downtime, and a reversible migration path.

Goals and success criteria:
- All customer private deployments can optionally be configured to use an HSM-backed root/key-encryption-key (KEK) for envelope encryption within 6 months.
- No plaintext secrets stored in Terraform state or in S3 buckets unencrypted.
- Audit events for key operations (create/rotate/destroy/access) are delivered to central SIEM within 5 minutes.
- Rollout pattern supports pilot -> staged rollout -> full opt-in with ability to revert.

Scope (in scope):
- Integration with external HSMs via PKCS#11 and cloud KMS providers where available.
- Terraform provider changes (vault, aws, google, pkcs11 where applicable) and module updates.
- Migration plan for secrets backplane (Vault/Transit -> new KEK-wrapped secrets).
- Audit log collection + signed integrity verification of key operations.

Non-goals (out of scope for v0.1):
- Building a proprietary HSM appliance image.
- Replacing customer-managed HSMs; we will integrate with their existing HSMs where possible.

Assumptions:
- Customers have at least one reachable, secured network path (VPN/Direct Connect) to our control plane or we will run a lightweight control plane proxy in-customer.
- Existing Vault Transit layer is available and can be extended to use external KEKs.
- Terraform state is stored in remote backends with encryption-at-rest (S3/GCS) but some tfvars still contain secrets that must be removed/migrated.

Target architecture (textual):
- Root key lives in HSM (customer HSM or cloud KMS HSM-backed key).
- Application secrets are encrypted using per-service data keys (DEKs) generated by Vault/Transit. DEKs are wrapped by the HSM KEK (envelope encryption).
- Terraform sensitive values are turned into a secrets resource and only store ciphertext (with metadata: key-id, wrapping-key-fingerprint).
- A short-lived cache of unwrapped DEKs exists in a dedicated, ephemeral instance only for rolling updates; never persisted to S3 or long-lived storage.
- Key operation audit logs: HSM -> collector -> signed transport -> SIEM (retention policies applied according to compliance tier).

Terraform module notes and patterns:
- New module: modules/crypto/hsm-kek-wrapper (inputs: hsm_connector, key_name, key_policy, allowed_principals). Outputs: kek_id, kek_fingerprint, kms_provider_meta.
- Provide an abstraction module modules/secrets/envelope that accepts a wrapping_key reference (kek_id) and returns ciphertext blobs and metadata.
- Avoid embedding secrets in tfvars. Pattern: terraform apply reads a secrets manifest (separate secured file) and calls an enrollment job (CI task) that stores ciphertext into a secrets data resource.
- Providers: keep explicit version pins. Example: hashicorp/vault v3.x, custom/hashicorp-pkcs11 v0.2.x (if using pkcs11 provider), aws v4.x (if AWS KMS used). Document exact provider versions in modules/crypto/versions.tf.
- Remote state: ensure state is encrypted and access-limited. Use workspace-level ACLs and never grant write to service accounts that do not need it.
- State migration: for resources that previously stored plaintext-like sensitive outputs, create a migration plan to re-encrypt and replace the state entry atomically (see "state migration steps" below).
- CI/CD: add a pre-apply check to ensure no cleartext secrets in plan output. Block merges that expose secrets in PR logs.

Terraform upgrade and migration steps (high level):
Phase 0: Discovery (2 weeks)
- Inventory all terraform stacks in private deployments that reference vault_secrets, aws_kms, or have sensitive tfvars. Map owners.
- Produce a table: stack, region, backend, sensitive_flag, current_key_provider.

Phase 1: Module rollout to dev/staging (4 weeks)
- Publish modules/crypto/hsm-kek-wrapper v0.1 and modules/secrets/envelope v0.1 to registry.
- Run integration tests in isolated dev, ensure module outputs usable by Vault/Terraform.
- Validate PKCS#11 connectors with test HSM (lab HSM or cloud HSM emulation).

Phase 2: Pilot (customer-embedded) (4–6 weeks)
- Choose 2 pilot customers (one cloud-HSM, one on-prem HSM).
- Work with customer infra to provision connector and network path.
- Migrate a low-risk service: create new KEK in HSM and rewrap a single DEK; update service to use rewrapped ciphertext.
- Monitor audit logs and rotate back if issues.

Phase 3: Staged rollout and general availability (ongoing)
- Gradually migrate other secrets and terraform stacks following a pre-approved migration checklist.
- Offer optional professional services to customers that require hands-on migration.

State migration steps (detailed):
- Lock state (terraform state lock).
- Add new resources that store ciphertext instead of plaintext.
- Run an off-line tool (migration helper) that:
  1) pulls plaintext secret from Vault/old store only in memory,
  2) calls HSM KEK to wrap a generated DEK,
  3) writes ciphertext and metadata to new secrets resource,
  4) updates references in application config to point to new ciphertext resource.
- Re-run terraform plan/apply to reconcile final state.
- Verify via acceptance tests.
- Release lock.

Rollback plan:
- Keep previous (unwrapped or old-wrapped) DEKs available for 48–72 hours after migration in an escrow location that is itself KEK-wrapped but accessible to our ops team under stricter auditing.
- If errors observed, run automated revert that swaps config back to previous secret reference (using tf apply with a pinned statefile snapshot).
- If corruption of ciphertext detected, escalate to incident response and do forensics on HSM audit trail.

Testing and acceptance criteria (automated):
- Unit tests for modules that mock PKCS#11 and verify wrap/unwrap semantics.
- Integration tests: create KEK in test HSM -> generate DEK -> encrypt data -> decrypt data via wrapped/unwrapped path.
- E2E smoke: run a rolling deploy that updates service to new secret reference with zero downtime target < 5m for small services.
- Audit verification: events for key-create/key-wrap/key-unwrap are present in SIEM within 5 minutes and include expected fields (principal, key-id, operation, request-id).

Audit logs and integrity:
- Signed audit chain: collector must sign batches of audit events using an ingestion key; ingestion layer validates signature and stores append-only logs.
- Retention: default 90 days in hot storage, 7 years in cold immutable storage for enterprise customers (configurable).
- Tamper detection: periodic integrity proofs (Merkle-root snapshots) recorded on an external tamper-evident ledger (optional customer opt-in).
- Fields: timestamp, principal, src_ip, operation, key_id, request_id, operation_result, context_tags.

Operational runbooks (incidents):
- HSM unreachable: -> switch to soft-KMS mode (if allowed by policy) with a forced read-only period; notify security and escalate.
- Key compromise suspected: -> revoke KEK, trigger rewrap of DEKs with a new KEK, require full application redeploy. Follow Key Compromise SOP (link in Confluence).
- Audit gaps: notify SRE, enable augmented logging, hold potential rollbacks for any affected migration windows.

Open questions / tradeoffs:
- Customer-managed HSM vs Redwood-hosted dedicated HSM: customers will choose; we need clear docs and an onboarding flow for both.
- Offline key ceremony tooling: do we provide a Redwood CLI helper for ceremonies or rely on customer tooling?
- Vault vs direct HSM wrapping: using Vault Transit provides better developer ergonomics but adds a layer; direct wrap reduces complexity for some customers. Plan to support both patterns.
- How to handle multi-tenant controllers in Dedicated clusters where a single HSM needs restricted per-tenant access.

Next actions (short-term):
- [Maya] Draft module interfaces and acceptability tests (2 weeks).
- [Liam] Stand up lab HSM and PKCS#11 connector for integration tests (1 week).
- [Ritika] Inventory terraform stacks and collect owner list (2 weeks).
- Schedule working session with security and SRE to finalize retention and SIEM schema (next week).

Owners and timeline (rough):
- Module dev: eng-private-deployments (Maya, Liam) — Q1 2026 pilot readiness.
- Pilot engineering + customer pilot coordination: solutions-engineering (Ritika, Hector) — pilot start Q1 2026.
- Audit/Logging and IR: eng-observability + security (Ellen) — ingestion pipe finished Q1 2026.

Appendix: helpful commands and small snippets (working):
- Example: pks11 connector test (pseudo):
  openssl pkcs11 -engine pkcs11 -keyform ENGINE -in /dev/null -sign -key 0x1234

- Migration helper conceptual (python):
  1) auth to old vault transit, fetch secret (in memory only)
  2) request HSM wrap: create DEK -> wrap with KEK -> receive ciphertext + metadata
  3) write ciphertext to new secrets path via Vault or TF resource API

References:
- Confluence: https://confluence.redwood.ai/pages/viewpage.action?pageId=11223344 (design notes)
- TF module PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/terraform-modules/pull/412
- Jira tickets: PD-789 (rollout epic), PD-790 (lab HSM infra)
